headline: High: Devin’s broad write/network/MCP autonomy can conflict with Authelia’s OAuth/ForwardAuth role, creating dangerous default-path data and action coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can process OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect and ForwardAuth traffic, while Devin can use MCP servers and browser/shell autonomy. If Authelia forwards untrusted content into Devin’s workspace or prompts, Devin may treat it as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty keeps it at medium.
conditions: IF Authelia forwards user-controlled headers or page content into Devin’s task context, injection becomes plausible.
IF Devin consumes forwarded content as instructions without provenance checks, the pathway is active.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all forwarded content.
Strip instruction-like text from forwarded headers/body.
Require Devin to treat ForwardAuth/OIDC payloads as data only.
Disable MCP ingestion for auth-related tasks.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tagging between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia handles authentication flows and broad network egress, while Devin reads/writes cloud workspace files, repo clones, and sends data to GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion/MCP. If Authelia or its auth logs expose secrets or identity data into Devin’s workspace, Devin’s default integrations can exfiltrate them onward. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Authelia logs or forwards tokens, claims, or headers into a shared workspace, Devin can read them.
IF Devin syncs that workspace to GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion, sensitive data can leave the original boundary.
mitigations: Redact tokens and headers before any handoff.
Keep auth logs outside Devin-accessible workspaces.
Disable Devin integrations for auth-related repos.
Rotate any secrets that may have been exposed.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and secret-scanning on shared artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/ForwardAuth surfaces, while Devin has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress. They can both affect shared mutable resources if pointed at the same repo or integration, but the profiles do not prove a shared directory or lockless orchestrator. That uncertainty prevents high severity.
conditions: IF both agents are configured against the same Git repository or workspace, write conflicts are possible.
IF no external locking exists, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches.
Pause one agent during the other’s write phase.
Use branch protection and required reviews.
Add a simple lock file or lease check.
requires-engineering: implement orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions and Devin is an autonomous planner-executor with browser, shell, and write access. If Devin treats Authelia’s outputs as authoritative, it can propagate a mistaken auth or policy decision into commits, tickets, or messages. The downstream action authority in Devin makes the blast radius potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Devin uses Authelia outputs as ground truth without verification, errors cascade.
IF Devin is allowed to act on those outputs in GitHub, Slack, Jira, or files, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require a human review step before Devin acts.
Have Devin cross-check auth outputs against a second source.
Limit Devin to draft-only actions for auth-related tasks.
Log and diff all downstream actions.
requires-engineering: add policy gates for high-impact actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service with no data classes listed, while Devin explicitly touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens. If identity or auth artifacts flow from Authelia into Devin’s cloud workspace or third-party integrations, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF Authelia-derived identity data is stored in Devin’s workspace or integrations, retention policy mismatch becomes relevant.
IF the deployment spans regulated data classes, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep auth artifacts out of Devin-managed tools.
Set short retention on shared tickets and chat.
Restrict Devin to non-sensitive repos.
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings.
requires-engineering: map data flows and retention controls end-to-end.
